regimes.name: Self-employed / sole proprietor (Schedule C, SE tax)
regimes.appliesTo: Independent contractors and sole proprietors with net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more; single filer modelled

incomeTax.base: taxable income = net profit minus half of SE tax minus standard deduction (federal only, single filer)

socialContributions.name: Self-employment tax: Medicare
socialContributions.base: 92.35% of net earnings from self-employment (extra 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax above $200,000 for single filers)

regimes.reserveBasis: At about 60,000 USD net profit: SE tax around 8,500 USD plus federal income tax around 4,500 USD is roughly 21-22% of gross; rounded to 2200.
regimes.notes: Federal only: state and local income taxes and state sales tax are NOT modelled. Standard deduction 16,100 USD for single filers in 2026 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32). Qualified business income deduction, credits and itemised deductions not modelled. The OASDI wage base for 2026 is 184,500 USD (SSA/Federal Register, confirmed via search results; ssa.gov page itself returned 403). Deadlines are the standard IRS dates and were not re-fetched; Jan 15 instalment falls in the following calendar year.

regimes.name: Self-employed / sole proprietor (T2125, CPP self-employed)
regimes.appliesTo: Sole proprietors and independent contractors; federal tax modelled, provincial tax not

incomeTax.base: net business income minus deductions (federal brackets only, before non-refundable credits)

socialContributions.name: CPP base contribution (self-employed, both halves)
socialContributions.base: net self-employment earnings between basic exemption 3,500 and YMPE 74,600 CAD

socialContributions.name: CPP2 (second additional contribution, self-employed)
socialContributions.base: self-employment earnings between 74,600 CAD (YMPE) and 85,000 CAD (YAMPE)

regimes.reserveBasis: At about 60,000 CAD net: CPP about 6,700 CAD plus federal tax around 5,500 CAD gives roughly 20% of gross before provincial tax; provincial tax would add more.

deadlines.name: Self-employed return filing (balance owing due April 30)

regimes.notes: Federal brackets only: provincial or territorial income tax (and Quebec QPP/QST) is NOT modelled. Federal lowest rate is 14% for the full 2026 year. allowanceMinor is the 2026 basic personal amount maximum 16,452 CAD, a non-refundable credit at the 14% rate rather than a deduction, taken from secondary sources (CRA page not reachable); it phases down for net income above 181,440 CAD. CPP: CRA confirms 2026 YMPE 74,600, basic exemption 3,500, base self-employed maximum 8,460.90 CAD; CPP2 8% and 85,000 YAMPE (max 832 CAD) are from secondary sources. Half of CPP is deductible. GST small supplier threshold 30,000 CAD and 5% GST rate and filing dates are from general CRA rules, not re-fetched.

legalForms.name: Société en nom collectif à responsabilité limitée

regimes.name: Monotributo (Regimen Simplificado para Pequenos Contribuyentes)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals and small partnerships with annual gross income up to the Category K ceiling (ARS 126,610,838.75 for services/goods per sources); categories A to K, recategorised every six months

incomeTax.base: income tax and VAT are included in a single fixed monthly fee by category

socialContributions.name: Monotributo monthly fee (tax plus pension plus health), Category A shown
socialContributions.base: fixed monthly amount by category; Category A 49,527.18 ARS per month, Category K 1,614,446.04 ARS (services) or 702,103.24 ARS (goods)

regimes.reserveBasis: Fee is fixed by category: about 5% of the Category A ceiling (49,527 ARS x 12 vs 12,009,410 ARS) up to about 15% for Category K services (1,614,446 x 12 vs 126,610,839); 8% is a mid-range rule of thumb.
regimes.notes: Scale reported as valid from 1 August 2026 (some sources say July to December 2026); figures come from press and calculator sites because the ARCA table could not be opened, so verify against ARCA. Only Categories A and K were captured; intermediate categories are not listed. fixedAnnualMinor is Category A x 12 = 594,326.16 ARS. Monthly due day 20 is general knowledge and unverified. General regime (responsable inscripto / Ganancias) not modelled.

regimes.name: Microempreendedor Individual (MEI)
regimes.appliesTo: Individual micro-entrepreneurs with annual gross revenue up to BRL 81,000, at most one employee, listed MEI activities

incomeTax.base: income tax, social security and ISS/ICMS collapsed into a fixed monthly DAS-MEI

socialContributions.name: DAS-MEI: INSS portion (5% of minimum wage 1,621) plus ISS (5 BRL) and/or ICMS (1 BRL)
socialContributions.base: fixed monthly amount: 81.05 BRL INSS plus 5 BRL ISS (services) and/or 1 BRL ICMS (goods)

regimes.reserveBasis: DAS-MEI is about 86 BRL per month; at a modest 4,000 BRL per month that is 2.2%, and at the 6,750 BRL monthly ceiling 1.3%; 3% leaves headroom for annual income tax on the taxable share of turnover.
regimes.notes: fixedAnnualMinor = (81.05 + 5.00) x 12 = 1,032.60 BRL (services activity). Truck-driver MEI pays more (194.52 BRL INSS). Due dates 20th and 31 May are general rules, not re-fetched. Sources are the Receita Simples Nacional notice and press; official page not opened directly. Simples Nacional (Annex III/IV) not modelled.

regimes.name: Autonomo / Pessoa Fisica (carne-leao plus INSS contribuinte individual)
regimes.appliesTo: Self-employed individuals without MEI registration, taxed as individuals

incomeTax.base: annualised monthly progressive table (monthly brackets x 12) on net professional income after INSS and allowed deductions; Law 15.270/2025 reduction not embedded

socialContributions.name: INSS contribuinte individual (normal plan)
socialContributions.base: monthly income between minimum wage 1,621 and ceiling 8,475.55 BRL

socialContributions.name: INSS simplified plan (alternative)
socialContributions.base: minimum wage only, 1,621 BRL; limited benefits

regimes.reserveBasis: At 6,000 BRL per month: INSS 20% (1,200) plus income tax about 230 after the Law 15.270 reduction is roughly 24%; with the 11% INSS plan about 15%; 22% used.
regimes.notes: From 1 Jan 2026 Law 15.270/2025 gives a monthly reduction: income tax is zero up to 5,000 BRL per month and phases out (reduction = 978.62 - 0.133145 x income) up to 7,350 BRL; not embedded in the brackets. Monthly simplified discount 607.20 BRL. Brackets from PwC (monthly table 2,428.80 / 2,826.65 / 3,751.05 / 4,664.68). Teto INSS 8,475.55 BRL and minimum wage 1,621 BRL from secondary sources. ISS municipal tax not modelled. Due dates are general rules, not re-fetched.

regimes.name: Trabajador independiente con boleta de honorarios (Impuesto Global Complementario)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals issuing boletas de honorarios (professional services) taxed as individuals

incomeTax.base: annual net taxable income (gross honorarios less 30% presumed expenses up to the statutory cap or actual expenses); AT 2026 table, amounts in whole pesos

socialContributions.name: Pension and health contributions for independent workers
socialContributions.base: share of honorarios income (rate and cap not verified)

regimes.reserveBasis: Withholding on boletas is 15.25% in 2026 per the statutory schedule (not re-verified) and is refunded against final tax; with 1.5M CLP per month income tax is about 2% so 15% (withholding) is the cash to hold back; value kept at 15%.
regimes.notes: CLP is modelled in whole pesos (ISO 4217 exponent 0), NOT multiplied by 100. Brackets are the SII Impuesto Global Complementario table for tax year 2026 (13.5 UTA exempt = 11,265,804 CLP; UTA 834,504). Social contribution rates and the 15.25% withholding rate were not verified (search was rate-limited). Boleta de honorarios is generally not subject to IVA. Pro Pyme regime (14 D) not modelled.

regimes.name: Impuesto de renta ordinario - persona natural independiente (cedula general)
regimes.appliesTo: Resident individuals earning fees or business income, who declare under the ordinary regime

incomeTax.base: renta liquida gravable after deductions and the 25% exempt labour income rule; Article 241 table in UVT (UVT 52,374 COP in 2026)

socialContributions.name: Health (EPS)
socialContributions.base: IBC = 40% of monthly income, minimum 1 SMMLV (1,750,905 COP)

socialContributions.name: Pension
socialContributions.base: IBC = 40% of monthly income, minimum 1 SMMLV (1,750,905 COP)

regimes.reserveBasis: Social security is about 28.5% of 40% of income, i.e. 11.4% of gross; income tax is zero below roughly 1,090 UVT (57.1M COP) taxable, so 14% covers social security with a small margin.
regimes.notes: Art. 241 bracket structure (0/19/28/33/35/37/39% with thresholds 1,090/1,700/4,100/8,670/18,970/31,000 UVT) is the long-standing table; search confirmed 7 brackets, 0% up to 1,090 UVT and 39% above 31,000 UVT, intermediate thresholds not re-verified this session. A pending bill (PL 477/2026) would change it but is not in force. Filing window depends on NIT digits (Aug-Oct 2026); day 31/month 8 is a placeholder not verified. Solidarity fund (extra 1% above 4 SMMLV), ARL, IBC ceiling (25 SMMLV) and the VAT responsibility threshold were not verified. SMMLV 2026 1,750,905 COP from press.

regimes.name: Regimen Simple de Tributacion (RST) - professional and consulting services
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals and companies with gross income below 100,000 UVT; professional/consulting/scientific services group

incomeTax.base: gross annual turnover; consolidated rate replaces income tax and ICA (municipal), annual rates by revenue band

socialContributions.name: Pension contribution (outside SIMPLE)
socialContributions.base: IBC = 40% of monthly income, minimum 1 SMMLV

regimes.reserveBasis: 5.9% SIMPLE rate on the first 6,000 UVT of turnover plus pension and health on 40% of income (about 11.4% of gross) is roughly 17%.
regimes.notes: Rates 5.9/7.3/12/14.5% by band come from secondary sources and could not be matched with the official text; conflicting source seen. Advance payments are actually bimonthly; the deadline entry is approximate and unverified. Health contribution not listed separately here. Bogota ICA is included in the consolidated rate but ICA differs by municipality.

regimes.name: Persona fisica con actividades lucrativas (independiente)
regimes.appliesTo: Self-employed individuals and sole proprietors earning profit from lucrative activities

incomeTax.base: annual net profit (income less deductible expenses); 2026 brackets under Executive Decree 45333-H

regimes.reserveBasis: Income tax is 0% up to 6.244M CRC net profit and 10-25% above; CCSS contributions (not verified) add roughly 10% on top; 10% is an estimate of CCSS only at modest income.
regimes.notes: EY states the 0% exempt amount for lucrative activities is 6,244,000 CRC for 2026. CCSS rate, 13% VAT, filing date and quarterly advance payments are not verified. Simplified tax regime for small taxpayers not researched. Reserve rate is a rough placeholder, mostly unverified.

regimes.name: Trabajador independiente - renta de cuarta categoria (recibos por honorarios)

incomeTax.base: annual labour income after allowances, UIT 5,500 PEN; rates by UIT band

regimes.reserveBasis: Taxable income after the 7 UIT allowance (38,500 PEN) is small at modest income, so tax is about 1-3% of gross; the usual 8% withholding on recibos por honorarios is a refundable advance, 8% retained as reserve.
regimes.notes: Brackets (8/14/17/20/30% at 5/20/35/45 UIT) and 7 UIT allowance from PwC; extra 3 UIT for deductible spending mentioned there. The 20% deduction for fourth category (cap 24 UIT) and the 8% withholding were not verified in this session. Fourth-category earners generally cannot use RUS/RER. Filing day/month is a placeholder. Mandatory pension for independents not verified.

regimes.name: Nuevo RUS (Nuevo Regimen Unico Simplificado)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals with business income up to 96,000 PEN per year (8,000 PEN per month); not for professional services

incomeTax.base: fixed monthly fee replaces income tax and IGV

socialContributions.name: Monthly fee: Category 1 (up to 5,000 PEN monthly) 20 PEN, Category 2 (up to 8,000 PEN) 50 PEN

regimes.reserveBasis: Fee is 20-50 PEN per month, 0.4-0.6% of the category ceiling; 1% leaves margin.
regimes.notes: fixedAnnualMinor is Category 1 (20 x 12 PEN); Category 2 is 600 PEN per year. Due dates depend on RUC digit and were not collected.

regimes.name: Regimen Especial de Renta (RER)
regimes.appliesTo: Individuals and companies with annual income and purchases up to 525,000 PEN, up to 10 workers, listed activities
regimes.reserveBasis: 1.5% monthly income tax on turnover; IGV collected on sales is a pass-through; 3% adds a margin for IGV timing.
regimes.notes: Fixed assets limit 126,000 PEN. IGV 18% (16% plus 2% IPM) is general knowledge, not verified here. Due dates not collected.

regimes.name: IRPF categoria II - independent professional (labour income)
regimes.appliesTo: Self-employed professionals taxed under IRPF progressive scale on labour income

incomeTax.base: annual taxable labour income; scale as of 31 Dec 2025 (BPC-indexed, may be revised in 2026)

regimes.reserveBasis: Not derived: BPS contribution rates and deductions were not verified, so no reserve rate is proposed.
regimes.notes: Scale from PwC (resident individuals, 31 Dec 2025). BPC value, IRPF category I (business income) rate, IVA and BPS rates not verified. Monotributo (BPS) and Literal E (minimum VAT, around 5,910 UYU per month per one source) exist but figures conflict between sources and were not captured.

regimes.name: Self-employed / sole trader (no direct taxation)
regimes.appliesTo: Any individual; Cayman levies no income, capital gains or withholding tax on individuals
regimes.reserveBasis: No income tax or VAT; nothing to reserve for tax under this model.
regimes.notes: Trade and business licence fees, work permit fees and National Pensions Scheme contributions may apply but were not verified and are not modelled. No VAT/sales tax per Carey Olsen.

regimes.name: Self-employed / sole proprietor (income tax on business profit)
regimes.appliesTo: Resident individuals carrying on a business; profit taxed under individual income tax (not profit tax)

incomeTax.base: annual taxable income in XCG, rates include 25% surtax

regimes.reserveBasis: At about 60,000 XCG taxable the scale gives roughly 9,600 XCG (about 16%) before allowances; social insurance not included because not verified.
regimes.notes: Currency is the Caribbean guilder (XCG), which replaced the ANG per Deloitte. 5% is the BBO sales tax standard rate; registration threshold not verified. Individual return is due two months after it is received from the tax office; no fixed date, so deadlines are empty. Personal allowances exist but amounts were not verified.
